checks.name: npm-version-published
checks.measured: 18 versions published, latest 0.3.0 — and no tag v0.3.1 exists, so the release has not been cut
checks.why: the version this tree calls itself must exist on the registry, or the tree is describing a release nobody can install

checks.name: npm-latest-is-the-release
checks.measured: latest=0.3.0 · tree=0.3.1 — and no tag v0.3.1 exists, so the release has not been cut
checks.why: a published version that is not `latest` installs for nobody who types the package name; a bumped version that was never cut leaves latest behind, which is exactly the state this check was written to catch

checks.name: npm-tarball-serves
checks.why: registry metadata can name a tarball the CDN does not serve; only fetching it proves an install would work

checks.name: npm-bytes-match-integrity
checks.why: the bytes a consumer receives must be the bytes the registry signed, recomputed here from what was served

checks.name: npm-shasum-matches
checks.why: the legacy digest is what older clients verify, and a release complete for new clients only is not complete

checks.name: npm-tarball-complete
checks.measured: the registry carries no dist for 0.3.1
checks.why: an empty or unexpanding tarball publishes successfully and installs nothing; unpacked must exceed compressed

checks.name: npm-provenance-attested
checks.measured: not attempted — the registry did not answer
checks.why: the publish claims a signed Sigstore provenance chain; an attestation URL that serves nothing makes that claim unverifiable

checks.name: zenodo-version-deposited
checks.measured: 17 versioned records in the chain, newest 0.3.0 — and no tag v0.3.1 exists, so the release has not been cut
checks.why: the archive is where the release is permanent; a release absent from it is citable by nobody, and the deposit job can be skipped or fail long after npm has already accepted the publish

checks.name: zenodo-record-carries-a-file
checks.measured: no record for this version — and no tag v0.3.1 exists, so the release has not been cut
checks.why: a published Zenodo record with no file is a landing page, not an archive — and it publishes just as successfully

checks.name: zenodo-doi-resolves
checks.measured: no Zenodo record for this version — nothing to resolve
checks.why: DataCite registration lags the deposit, so a record can exist while its DOI resolves nowhere; a citation that 404s is worse than no citation because it looks like one

checks.name: npm-and-zenodo-agree
checks.why: the code a reader installs and the record they cite must be the same release; the two publish independently, so they drift apart silently whenever one of the two halves of a release fails
